item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Nov 10, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/

item.title: Building & Publishing Your Webpage with Codex — Tue Nov 10, 1:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
Ever wanted to build your own website but weren't sure where to start? In this beginner-friendly 2-hour workshop, you'll create your very own one-page website and put it online for the world to see-no experience needed! With the help of Codex, a smart AI assistant that writes code for you, you'll bring your ideas to life just by describing what you want. item.title: Civic Health in North Carolina: Using Data to Build for the Future — Tue Nov 10, 2:00 PM — Wellness Center
item.description:
Since 2003, North Carolina's Civic Health Index has offered a window into how people connect, participate, and contribute to their communities' civic life. The data tell a complex story: North Carolina faces persistent gaps in civic and political participation, but alongside those challenges are important strengths and bright spots that point toward what is possible. In this interactive session, led by Leslie Garvin, Executive Director of North Carolina Campus Engagement (NCCE) at Elon University, we'll look at the 2024 and 2026 data and explore what they reveal about our state's civic life. Together, we'll consider how this information is helping identify the civic assets we can build on and the opportunities to strengthen civic health from the local level to the state.
Register at the link.
Source: Duke University

item.title: The Ethics of Now with Lewis Akenji — Fri Nov 13, 7:00 PM — Durham County Main Library
item.description: Join the Kenan Institute for Ethics and host Adriane Lentz-Smith for a conversation with Lewis Akenji on reorienting the economy to fight climate change and promote human wellbeing. Whether pushing environments to new extremes, fracturing local economies, or heightening social tensions, climate change is impacting us all — but the way we talk about it is not leading us towards solutions. Lewis Akenji says we tend to focus on consumerist lifestyles rather than the economic structures that drive these behaviors in the first place — and the kind of society we want to build instead. Join Akenji to explore how we can regain our agency around climate change by acting as collectives instead of individuals, and how, as communities and governments, we can address the interlinked crises of climate change and economic insecurity in ways that promote human wellbeing. There are giggles and surprises behind every door, and lots of chances to get involved with the action. Created by Olivia Aston Bosworth and Samantha Provenzano Commissioned by Alliance Theatre Originally developed and produced by the Alliance Theatre (Atlanta, GA) as part of the Kathy and Ken Bernhardt Theatre for the Very Young series. item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Feb 6, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description: The Islamic Secular argues that the common notion of a fundamental conflict between the secular and the religious cannot be applied to Islam. This is not because Islam rejects the secular in favor of the religious; it is because Islam's concept of the religious includes the secular. This is what is captured by the term "Islamic Secular." Contrary to both the notion that "religion" in Islam equals "sharī'ah," and to the concomitant notion that sharī'ah is the all-encompassing, exclusive metric of assessment in Islam, this book argues that, while Islam is all-encompassing, sharī'ah is bounded. This leaves a space between the limited circumference of sharī'ah and the unlimited circumference of Islam. While both spaces are "religious" in that they come under the adjudicative gaze of the God of Islam, only the shar'ī space draws directly upon sharī'ah and its sources, while the non-shar'ī space does not. item.title: Elvira Notari: Oltre il silenzio – Film Screening and Discussion with Director Valerio Ciriaci — Mon Nov 9, 7:00 PM — None
item.description:
Join us for a screening of Elvira Notari: Oltre il silenzio (Awen Films, 2025), presented at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival, followed by a conversation with director Valerio Ciriaci.
Elvira Notari was Italy's first woman film director. From her studio in Naples, Dora Film, she wrote, directed and produced dozens of feature films in the 1910s and 1920s: popular melodramas shot in the streets of the city, with a realism that anticipated later Italian cinema. Most of her work has been lost, and her name was nearly erased from film history. Ciriaci's documentary follows the traces she left behind and asks what it means to recover a filmmaker from silence.
Introductions by Hank Okazaki and Tania Rispoli. Discussion to follow with Tom Whiteside (Director of Durham Cinematheque) and Roberto Dainotto (Professor of Literature).

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations.
